title: Risk and Treasury Memorandum: The Concentration Limit on a Customer's Certificate of Deposit Principal
content:
Certificates of Deposit are combined for one purpose only, a limit on how much certificate principal one customer of Piedmont Crescent Bank may hold. This memorandum states that limit and, equally, the purposes for which balances are never combined.

## 1. The limit

1.1 The customer's total certificate principal, measured as the sum of the principal standing on all of that customer's certificates whose status is not closed, plus the deposit being made, must not exceed 2500000.00 USD.

1.2 The measure is taken at close of business on the day of the opening or the deposit.

1.3 An opening or an add-on that would breach the limit is declined. It is never reduced to a sum that would fit.

1.4 Interest compounded into a certificate may take the total above the limit, and that carries no consequence.

## 2. What is never combined

Balances are never combined for pricing. The jumbo bonus is judged on each certificate's own principal at its term start, and two certificates can never be added together to reach a tier's jumbo principal figure.

## 3. Evidence and timing

The total is read from the bank's own certificate records before the action, over the certificates that name the customer as owner. It is not taken from the customer's statement of what they hold.

## 4. Boundary and worked readings

A customer whose certificates not closed total 2450000.00 USD asks to open a certificate with 50000.00 USD. The sum is exactly 2500000.00 USD, which does not exceed the limit, so the opening proceeds. Asked instead for 60000.00 USD, the sum would be 2510000.00 USD, the limit is exceeded, and the opening is declined outright rather than cut back to 50000.00 USD.

A customer holding two certificates of 60000.00 USD each is not thereby brought to any jumbo principal figure: neither certificate is priced on the other's balance.
